sources.supports: addVariable validates the project identifier, posts to add_variable/{project_id} with the payload as the JSON body and parses the reply with VariableSchema. The payload is passed through unexamined: no public method parses AddVariablePayloadSchema, so every payload rule is enforced at the MCP boundary alone.

AddVariablePayloadSchema declares a single required name of type string and nothing else. VariableSchema declares the reply as exactly two required non-nullable fields, id and name; there is no value field, because a value belongs to a dataset.

add_variable creates a variable in a project; its parameter table carries project_id alone, marked required. The documented response fields are the id and name of the newly added variable. The documented 400 causes are an invalid or missing project_id, an invalid variable name, a variable name that already exists within the project, and exceeding the number of allowed variables. 403 covers insufficient project permissions, no add/edit permission for Test Data within the project, and "Not an Enterprise license/subscription". The example request body also shows an id, which the parameter table does not document.

input_policy.notes: One identifier in the path and a body of exactly one documented field. An unknown body field is refused, including the id the article's example shows and its parameter table never lists: TestRail assigns the identifier. Whether the name is free within the project is TestRail's rule and its refusal arrives from upstream.

outer_result.notes: TestRail answers with the created variable, which carries an identifier and a name only. Entity-field drift is advisory.

requirements.description: Reject unknown top-level fields before driver invocation rather than forwarding or discarding them.
Reject an unknown body field, including the id the article's example shows and TestRail assigns.

parameters.semantics: The project the variable is created in. No coercion; passed positionally and sent verbatim as the only path segment.

wire.encoding: Decimal integer path segment; numeric strings are rejected rather than coerced.

parameters.semantics: No coercion. The JSON object is passed as the driver's second argument and sent unchanged.

requirements.description: Preserve the object at driver argument 1 as the JSON request body.
Reject a body that is not an object before driver invocation.

parameters.semantics: The variable's name, which TestRail requires and which dataset write payloads later key their values by. No coercion; TestRail owns the format and the uniqueness rule within the project.

requirements.description: Preserve the value under its own name.
Reject a non-string value before driver invocation.
